premises.text: Clean-energy transition drives exploding lithium demand for batteries while brine holds most global lithium resources
premises.evidence_span: brines are the natural resources of lithium, which are present in the form of salt lake, continental brines, and oil field brines, constituting 66% of total global lithium resources

premises.text: Solar evaporation extraction is slow, water-intensive, carbon-emitting, and costly, so brine industry lacks efficient tech to meet battery demand
premises.evidence_span: to just produce one metric ton of lithium, they use up 500,000 gallons of water, releasing 5,000 kilograms of carbon, with a production cost of $6,000

premises.text: Nano-mosaic sponge-like absorbents selectively attract lithium and reject other minerals, enabling a two-step direct extraction to battery grade in about 48 hours with far less water, lower cost, and zero carbon
premises.evidence_span: nano-mosaic absorbents, which are very similar to a sponge. These sponge-like materials are chemically and physically designed to just attract lithium, rejecting all other minerals. So taking advantage of the selectivity, our process is just two-step. extracting lithium within 48 hours and process it into battery grade

premises.text: Room-temperature polyphenol absorbents in filter units scale to high throughput lithium extraction for brine and petrochemical operators
premises.evidence_span: These are made at room temperature from naturally available polyphenols. And here is our filter units, which can treat almost 171 gallons of water per minute, extracting two metric tons of lithium per day

premises.text: Current customers are lithium brine and petrochemical operators; tech can extend to other critical mineral extractions such as nickel and cobalt
premises.evidence_span: Our current customers are lithium brine operators. from lithium industry and petrochemical industries
